na536c463021d: Neural population geometry constrains how task variables are represented and read out into behavior. We propose a variational principle in which learning balances task accuracy and representational smoothness under stimulus-dependent weighting. This balance links stimulus statistics to the shape of a latent neural coordinate. For magnitude estimation, the principle predicts distortions near the edges of bounded ensembles, global affine contraction for Gaussian ensembles, and warping toward high-probability regions for bimodal ensembles. We test the bounded-uniform case in recurrent neural networks trained to reproduce time intervals. Their learned geometries occupy three regimes as the boundary distortions change from too narrow to resolve, to measurable, to extending across the stimulus range. A shape parameter selected from an empirical neural coordinate predicts the nonlinear component of mean behavior through an affine readout, with only behavioral gain and offset fitted afterward. In this bounded-uniform setting, the variational coordinate and Bayesian least-squares mean response have closely matching shapes after affine normalization. These results suggest a variational account of how stimulus statistics shape neural geometry and yield Bayesian-like behavior.
nc773d89d2607: Physiological markers measured at rest, such as heart rate variability, have proved relatively weak predictors of mental health symptoms. One potential reason is that resting measures are influenced by uncontrolled state factors, such as spontaneous breathing, whereas a standardized challenge holds these constant and may reveal regulatory differences not evident at rest. Here we asked whether respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) during slow paced breathing, a challenge that strongly increases RSA, carries information about symptoms beyond resting RSA and interoceptive measures. In 207 young adults (mean age 23.6 years, SD = 3.1), electrocardiogram (ECG) was recorded at rest and during slow (6 breaths/min) and fast (20 breaths/min) paced breathing. Lower RSA during slow breathing, relative to that predicted by resting RSA, was associated with more severe generalized anxiety symptoms ({beta} = -0.21, BF = 13), also when depressive symptoms were controlled, whereas resting RSA was not. The association was concentrated among participants with at least moderate anxiety symptoms, whose resting RSA was typical but whose rest-adjusted slow-breathing RSA was 0.62 SD lower, and who in exploratory analyses also showed weaker phase coupling between heart period and respiration. Interoceptive accuracy, measured with heartbeat counting or heart rate discrimination, was unrelated to symptoms, self-report and slow-breathing RSA, and interoceptive questionnaires tracked distress shared across anxiety and depressive symptoms rather than generalized anxiety symptoms. At the group level, slow-breathing RSA thus carries information about generalized anxiety symptoms beyond resting RSA and self-reported interoception. Brief paced-breathing challenges may therefore increase the sensitivity of autonomic markers in anxiety research and merit testing in clinical samples.
n0ffa224efe4b: Both spike processing efficiency and host protease usage play critical roles in SARS-CoV-2 infection, pathogenesis, and transmission. The SARS-CoV-2 spike contains two motifs, a furin cleavage site (FCS) and an extended S1/S2 loop, which improve both cleavage efficiency and host protease usage. Disruption of these motifs significantly attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection and pathogenesis. Importantly, modifications and changes within the S1/S2 loop can also shape infection and disease outcomes following infection. In this study, we examined mass spectrometry data generated from purified virions from wild-type (WT) or mutant SARS-CoV-2 infection. We identified phosphorylation occurring at highly conserved residue Y674 and used reverse genetics to generate a mutant that ablates phosphorylation capacity in the S1/ S2 loop (Y674F). Our results show that the Y674F mutant replicated equivalently to wild-type SARS-CoV-2 in Vero cells but had attenuated replication in a human respiratory cell line. Golden Syrian hamsters infected with the Y674F mutant had equivalent weight loss, lung viral titer, and similar immune pathology to WT SARS-CoV-2. However, the mutant had reduced viral load in the nasal wash and reduced antigen staining in the large airways in the lung. Notably, loss of Y674 ablated spike processing to the S1/S2 cleavage product on virions. In addition, Y674F mutant had a diminished capacity to utilize host protease TMPRSS2 for entry. Together, these data indicates that post-translational modification of Y674 impacts SARS-CoV-2 infection of the airway by disrupting both spike processing and host protease function. These results add to data demonstrating the importance of spike S1/S2 loop modifications to SARS-CoV-2 infection, pathogenesis, and transmission. ### Competing Interest Statement VDM has filed a patent on the reverse genetic system for SARS-CoV-2. All other authors declare no conflicts of interest. Other authors declare no competing interests. ndc6976a31da4: Cyclin-dependent kinase 12 (CDK12) is an attractive therapeutic target due to its critical role in transcriptional regulation and DNA damage response and is frequently co-amplified with ERBB2 (HER2) in breast cancer. CDK12 forms an active complex with its obligate partner cyclin K (CCNK), and pharmacological degradation of CCNK has emerged as a promising strategy for disrupting CDK12-dependent transcriptional programs. However, the broad expression and essential functions of the CDK12/CCNK complex may limit the therapeutic window of highly potent molecular glue degraders. Here, we investigate whether antibody-mediated delivery can impart cellular selectivity to a molecular glue degrader through targeting the HER2 receptor. Molecular glues lack the modular architecture of PROTACs, thus linker placement can be the central design problem. We designed SAS1001, a CCNK molecular glue degrader with a solvent-exposed piperazine primed for linker attachment. SAS1001 induced potent and ubiquitin-proteasome system-dependent degradation of CCNK and inhibited proliferation in a range of breast cancer cells. Conjugation to trastuzumab (Tz) generated the HER2-targeted degrader-antibody conjugate Tz-SS2009, which internalized preferentially in HER2-positive cells and produced enhanced CCNK degradation and antiproliferative effects, relative both to HER2-negative cells and to an isotype-matched non-targeting conjugate. Whole proteome analysis further demonstrated CCNK depletion and revealed downstream changes consistent with established roles of the CDK12/CCNK complex in transcriptional regulation. These findings demonstrate that antibody-mediated delivery can redistribute the cellular activity of a potent molecular glue degrader towards antigen-positive cells. In the CR8/DS18 purine series, substitution at a solvent-exposed position preserved CCNK degradation when the degrader was delivered on a full-length IgG. More broadly, this work extends antibody-directed degradation beyond the CRBN-based glues that have dominated the field and illustrates how structural characterization of a glue scaffold can identify a linker attachment point that does not compromise activity.
nb860a9efc28d: Alphaproteobacteria of the order Rickettsiales include biomedically important, yet understudied arthropod-borne human pathogens. These pathogens lack obvious morphological asymmetry, but encode homologs of key mediators of polar processes in the model Alphaproteobacterium Caulobacter crescentus. These include the polar organizing protein PopZ, the chromosome segregation proteins ParA and ParB, and the spatial regulator of cell division MipZ. Motivated by this observation, we used the tick-borne human pathogen Rickettsia parkeri to ask if the chromosome is polarized and coordinated with cell division in this group. Consistent with that hypothesis, we found that transposon insertion mutants in parA, parB, mipZ, or popZ resulted in cell division defects. Fluorescence imaging revealed cell cycle-dependent unipolar-to-bipolar localization dynamics of ParB and MipZ, and pole-to-midcell dynamics of the division protein ZapA. This patterning parallels the model of chromosome segregation and cell division site selection established in Caulobacter. Unlike its unipolar-to-bipolar dynamics in Caulobacter, however, PopZ remained at a single cell pole throughout the cell cycle in R. parkeri. PopZ maintained its direct interaction with ParA and ParB. Interestingly, disruption of parA or parB, but not popZ or mipZ, caused a small plaque phenotype, suggesting a defect in growth or spread in a monolayer of host cells in the absence of proper chromosome segregation. We propose that genome polarization in R. parkeri and other rickettsiae is critical both for fundamental cellular processes and for interactions with host cells that promote fitness in their infectious niche.
n61e86ab2de73: Acidification is a principal antimicrobial host defence: during infection, bacteria have to survive the stomach, the vaginal tract or the phagolysosome of immune cells, where the pH falls below 5. To persist, bacteria must sense and adapt to extracellular pH. In Gram-positive bacteria, the membrane protein CdaR, a regulator of the c-di-AMP-synthesizing enzyme CdaA, has been proposed as a pH sensor, but the molecular basis of this sensing remains unknown. Here we show, using the model organism Bacillus subtilis, that CdaR is essential for growth below pH 5. SEC-MALS, mass photometry and circular dichroism demonstrate that its extracellular YbbR domains neither oligomerize nor unfold at low pH. Instead, tryptophan and ANS fluorescence reveal a reversible conformational change that requires at least two tandem YbbR domains and occurs between pH 4.5 and 5.5. Crystallography, molecular dynamics and solution NMR localize this transition to a conserved hinge between YbbR domains 1 and 2, where a network of charged residues rearranges to rigidify it and restrict inter-domain motion. Mutagenesis identifies a highly conserved aspartate whose substitution abolishes the conformational switch in vitro and accelerates adaptation to low pH in vivo. These findings define a structural mechanism by which CdaR senses extracellular acidification through its YbbR domains and couples this signal to intracellular c-di-AMP signaling. As the hinge and its aspartate are the most conserved features of the YbbR family, found in pathogens including Staphylococcus aureus and Listeria monocytogenes, we propose this as a general mechanism of acid adaptation in Gram-positive bacteria.
n19b1cecca5b9: Background Adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) is widely used to improve microbial fitness under defined selective pressures. Mutations accumulated during ALE may interact epistatically, with the effect of one mutation depending on another. Understanding these interactions can help explain adaptive phenotypes and inform combinatorial strain engineering, but experimentally testing all mutation combinations is impractical. We developed a computational framework that uses gene-pair co-occurrence and mutual exclusivity patterns to identify candidates for experimental investigation of epistasis. Results We applied the framework to a curated compendium of 141 Escherichia coli ALE experiments from ALEdb, using the Fisher exact test and DISCOVER as complementary statistical screens. Testing and multiple-testing correction were performed separately within each experiment, method, and direction (co-occurrence and mutual exclusivity). At a 5% false discovery rate threshold, the Fisher exact test identified 74 significant gene pairs, comprising 36 co-occurrences and 38 mutual exclusivities. DISCOVER identified 5 significant pairs, all for mutual exclusivity and also significant under the Fisher exact test. These shared pairs suggested alternative adaptive routes involving temperature tolerance, glycerol utilization, and associations between RNA polymerase subunit genes. The two methods produced similar expected overlaps for Fisher-significant pairs, but the broader null distributions of DISCOVER yielded larger raw p-values. Of the 69 pairs significant only under the Fisher exact test, 60 arose in experiments with multiple strain labels or involved a gene with only one distinct mutation recorded across all affected endpoints (final samples from lineages evolved in parallel), highlighting the need to examine genetic backgrounds and mutation origins when interpreting the results. Power analysis indicated that the Fisher exact test required 70 independent endpoints for co-occurrence and 215 for mutual exclusivity to achieve 80% power under pre-specified scenarios. We implemented the framework as a reusable Nextflow pipeline that automates statistical screening of ALEdb and user-supplied mutation datasets. Conclusions By combining gene-pair screening with mutation-level interpretation, this reproducible framework narrows the search space for experimental investigation of epistasis and can contribute to combinatorial strain design. The power analysis provides sample-size benchmarks for planning future ALE experiments with adequate power to screen for candidate genetic interactions.
nd1fafff84805: Complementary dipeptides bearing the non-canonical nucleobases melamine and cyanuric acid (alpha DPNA) assemble into a cylindrical hexameric structure containing a stacked heterocyclic core with its beta-sheet peptide backbones on the surface. Circular dichroism spectroscopy and singular-value decomposition show that the evolution of CD spectra after mixing equimolar strands is an apparent two-state process, accounted for by only the spectra of free strands and the assembled hexamer, with no detectable intermediates. Equilibrium measurements reveal a highly cooperative, enthalpically driven assembly with a molecularity of 6.2 +/- 0.2 and an association constant of (2.3 +/- 0.2)X10^22 " " M^(-5). Over total strand concentrations of 20 to 100 micromolar, the assembly progress curves are described by an apparent reversible sixth-order macroscopic rate law. This deceptively simple behavior cannot represent an elementary six-strand collision. The apparent forward rate constant has a negative activation energy, showing that the observed rate law masks additional steps in the assembly reaction. A minimal model in which strand pre-isomerization precedes hexamer formation restores a physically reasonable positive activation energy while retaining the observed two-state CD behavior. Constrained simulations further show that a sequential pathway with low-population, spectroscopically silent, intermediates can give rise to the same deceptively simple sixth-order progress curve. These results provide an unusual example of highly cooperative hexamer formation and show how a simple high-order macroscopic rate law can conceal a more complex microscopic assembly mechanism. The thermodynamics and kinetics provide insights into how and why the hexamer assembles, offering some design principles for supramolecular assemblies in water.
n149cce379e0c: Mendel proposed the laws of segregation and independent combination in his study. However, he focused on "dominant" characters but left "intermediate" ones. Using genotypic and phenotypic data for four representative genes, we reveal connections between the "intermediate" and "dominant" characters. We demonstrate that the fundamental inheritance patterns of these genes are additive effects on both component and compound traits. Additive effects involving more than two genes generate non-additive effects in hybrids. For compound traits such as grain yield, their inheritance depends on differential patterns of component traits in parents; only parents with optimal balances of reciprocal differences in component traits produce overdominant effects, which is important for hybrid breeding. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. 2026 National Innovation Center for Salt-Tolerant and Alkali-Tolerant Rice Project, ZDYF2026GCZX001
ncc2453b86914: Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), including semaglutide, have transformed the pharmacological treatment of obesity. While highly efficacious in promoting weight loss, these drugs also induce substantial reductions in lean mass, raising concerns for skeletal muscle loss, particularly in older individuals vulnerable to sarcopenia. Nevertheless, there are currently no published human studies that investigated the effects of GLP-1RAs on skeletal muscle mass using gold standard methods. Meanwhile, studies in young mice demonstrate that skeletal muscle loss induced by GLP-1RAs might not be a major concern. The purpose of the current study was to investigate the effects of semaglutide on skeletal muscle mass and strength in aged mice. Methods Eighteen-month-old male and female C57BL/6J mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) for 12 weeks to induce obesity. At 21 months of age, mice received daily subcutaneous injections of vehicle or semaglutide (3 or 30 nmol/kg) for 3 weeks. Body composition was assessed weekly by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. After 3 wks, mice were terminated to assess masses of individual organs including skeletal muscle. Skeletal muscle force-generating capacity was assessed by ex vivo electrical stimulation-induced contraction. Myofiber cross-sectional area and fiber-type composition were also assessed. Results Semaglutide induced dose-dependent weight loss in both sexes, with reductions of 11.3% and 20.2% in males and 21.1% and 26.1% in females receiving 3 or 30 nmol/kg dose, respectively. There was a substantial sex-difference in the loss of lean mass, with relatively minor reductions in males (2.3% and 6.6%) and greater loss in females (8.6% and 8.3%). Skeletal muscle mass was largely preserved in males but females exhibited greater muscle mass loss, including 14.2% reduction in quadriceps mass at 30 nmol/kg of semaglutide treatment. In contrast, skeletal muscle force-generating capacity was not compromised in semaglutide-treated females, while males exhibited 19.2% reduction in force generating capacity of the extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles at the 30 nmol/kg dose. Conclusion Unlike young mice, semaglutide treatment may induce meaningful loss in skeletal muscle mass in aged female mice and muscle strength in aged male mice. These findings highlight the importance of considering age as a potential factor that may negatively influence muscle mass and function in humans treated with GLP-1RAs. Clinical studies examining the influence of pharmacological weight loss on skeletal muscle mass and strength should consider both age and sex as a potentially important determinant of these outcomes.
nc86abcd65ab0: Introduction: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), fibromyalgia (FM), and long COVID (LC-19) are chronic diseases with overlapping clinical features and poorly understood pathophysiology. Increasing evidence suggests the involvement of immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and altered vascular physiology. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are key mediators of intercellular communication and are envisioned as sensors of homeostasis and disease. The aim of this study was to determine whether EV marker profiling could provide a basis for the differential diagnosis of ME/CFS, FM and LC-19 and/or patient stratification. Methods: EV-enriched plasma from ME/CFS, FM, cases co-diagnosed with ME/CFS and FM, LC-19 patients, and matched healthy controls (n = 10 per study group) were analyzed. EV concentration and size distribution were assessed by nanoparticle tracking analysis, followed by targeted profiling of EV-associated surface markers via AlphaScreen, including tetraspanins CD9 and CD63, platelet- (CD41/CD61), myeloid- (CD13), immune- (CD74 and CX3CR1), and renin-angiotensin system- associated ACE1 (also known as CD143), and ACE2 surface markers. Results: The studied disease groups presented distinct EV signatures. LC-19 samples exhibited the most pronounced and coordinated alterations, characterized by increased levels of CD9/CD74, CD9/CX3CR1, and CD9/ACE1-positive EVs, along with reduced overall particle concentrations. Notably, platelet-derived CD9/CD41/CD61-positive EVs were significantly elevated in both LC-19 and ME/CFS, as compared to healthy controls, indicating enhanced platelet activation. Immune-associated markers revealed differential pathway activation in LC-19, with CD74-positive EVs reflecting antigen presentation and inflammatory signaling, and CX3CR1-positive EVs indicating altered leukocyte trafficking and vascular interaction. Increased ACE1-positive EVs in LC-19 further suggested a shift toward pro-inflammatory renin-angiotensin signaling. Conclusion: Collectively, these findings support a disease-specific dysregulation of platelet, immune, and vascular pathways. The integrated EV signatures distinguish LC-19 from the related chronic conditions ME/CFS and FM, highlighting the potential of EV-based profiling for differential diagnosis. Our results provide a systems-level perspective on the differential pathophysiology of these disorders and identify EV-associated markers as candidate biomarkers with clinical value.
n04e96da1b459: Mechanistically distinct neurodegenerative diseases result in similar cognitive deficits, and pathology is often concentrated in a set of circuits known to be selectively vulnerable. Selective vulnerability is an intrinsic property of a circuit: in APP/PS1 mice, where plaques are global, functional disruptions are confined to circuits within the default mode network. What characterizes the dynamics of vulnerable circuits from those of spared circuits is unknown. We asked whether the distinguishing property is the proximity of population dynamics to criticality, a homeostatic set-point of network activity that determines computational capacity. We recorded single units simultaneously in three selectively vulnerable regions (retrosplenial cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and CA1 hippocampus) and in primary visual cortex of freely behaving young and old APP/PS1 and wild-type mice. Firing rate and spike-time variability differed by genotype inconsistently across regions and ages. In contrast, three measures from criticality theory each revealed deficits that emerged only with age and only in the vulnerable regions. No measure detected a progressive change in V1. Avalanche scaling is not fixed in neural activity, but varies along a scaling line as the network state changes. As a result, the lines generated by each genotype revealed a constitutive effect of the transgene in young animals, which inverted with age in amyloid-bearing animals, but only in vulnerable circuits. If the destabilization of near-critical dynamics directly reflects a circuit's functional capacity, the same signature should identify a mechanistically distinct degenerative disease. In a model of tauopathy (P301S/E4), CA1 dynamics were displaced from the control scaling line with the same age-dependent reversal observed in APP/PS1. Our results suggest a network-level principle of neurodegenerative diseases: molecularly unrelated pathologies converge on the loss of near-critical dynamics in selectively vulnerable circuits.
n0cc5bb6694de: Dynamic RNA-protein interactions influence RNA transport, storage, stability, and activity and are fundamental to a broad range of biological processes. During the oocyte-to-embryo transition (OET), fully differentiated gametes fuse and regain totipotency. Throughout the OET, the transcription remains silent. Spatiotemporal regulation of gene expression relies on the dynamic interactions between maternal transcripts and various protein complexes. Despite its fundamental importance, RNA-protein interaction dynamics at the global level during the OET remain poorly understood. Here, we leverage fractionation RNA-seq to profile RNA insolubility, a proxy for the interaction between RNAs and protein complexes, during zebrafish OET. We identify transcripts that transition between the soluble (relatively protein-free) and insoluble (heavily protein-associated) states and demonstrate that these phase transitions are driven by ribosome-dependent and ribosome-independent mechanisms. We demonstrate that the capacity of maternal RNAs to engage with protein complexes changes dynamically during the OET through remodeling of cis-regulatory features. We developed a machine-learning framework and uncovered multiple cis- and trans-regulatory features that may contribute to RNA insolubility. To validate these predictions, we examined poly(A) tail length and m6A dynamics. We found that poly(A) tail length is associated with both ribosome-dependent and ribosome-independent RNA phase transitions. In parallel, fractionation m6A-pulldown RNA-seq revealed highly dynamic changes in the m6A landscape during the OET. A correlation between m6A modifications and RNA insolubility is gradually established during the OET. Together, our findings uncover a multilayered regulatory mechanism governing RNA phase transitions during the OET, providing fundamental insights into post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression during development. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nfed7b517cd61: Biallelic loss of MUTYH causes MUTYH-associated polyposis (OMIM: 608456), characterized by the oxidative base-excision-repair mutational signature SBS18, but whether the roughly 1 in 100 individuals who carry a single pathogenic MUTYH allele acquire a mutational phenotype in normal tissue is unknown. Analysis of multi-tissue sequencing of 25 donors from the Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network identified three heterozygous carriers of MUTYH p.Gly396Asp. One carrier showed SBS18 across multiple normal tissues, ranking first of 25 donors with three independent methods and remaining significant after adjustment for tissue, without a somatic, epigenetic or transcriptional second hit at the MUTYH locus. A single hypomorphic MUTYH allele can therefore leave a measurable oxidative mutational mark in healthy tissues, supporting tissue-level mutational readouts as an approach to cancer risk stratification within this common carrier state.
n4d18a84a8c56: The Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is an essential environmental sensor bridging metabolic cues with immune regulation, yet its precise role in defining human monocyte-derived macrophage identity remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that AhR functions as a critical transcriptional rheostat that selectively restrains the anti-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic identity of M-CSF-dependent monocyte-derived macrophages (M-Mac). Integrated ChIP-Seq and transcriptomic profiling revealed that AhR activity is enriched in M-Mac in a MAFB-dependent manner, directly occupying regulatory regions of core M-Mac identity genes, including CD163, LGMN, and IL10. Unexpectedly, siRNA-mediated knockdown and CRISPR/Cas9 ablation demonstrated that AhR primarily functions as a repressor; its deficiency accelerated and exacerbated the acquisition of a "resident-like" (LYVE1+/FOLR2+) and pro-fibrotic phenotype. Functionally, AhR restricted the M-Mac anti-inflammatory response to TLR7 ligation, and limited an overly tolerogenic profile during M-Mac-driven T-cell responses. Pharmacological modulation using the endogenous ligand FICZ and the antagonist SR1 confirmed that AhR activity limits the magnitude of the MAFB-driven program and the autocrine IL-10 signaling axis. Collectively, these findings establish AhR as a fundamental checkpoint that prevents macrophages from acquiring an excessive anti-inflammatory state, thereby ensuring balanced responses essential for tissue homeostasis and immune surveillance.
n4906037632fa: Do protein language models (pLMs) encode the physical rules that govern protein folding? The four-helix bundle provides a classic test case because binary patterning, the ordered placement of polar and nonpolar residues along an amphipathic α-helix, is sufficient to generate folded proteins with high probability. Here, we ask whether ESM2 captures the sequence grammar underlying this design strategy. Libraries of synthetic sequences constrained only by binary patterning were predicted by ESMFold to form four-helix bundles. Predicted helicity, compactness, and topological diversity changed with sequence length in the same direction as experimentally characterized libraries, although the model did not distinguish successful from unsuccessful individual designs. Principal component analysis of ESM2 embeddings revealed representations of hydrophobic patterning, helix-loop boundaries, and heptad register. Extending the analysis to all 128 heptad binary patterns produced a jellyfish-shaped manifold in which hydrophobic composition formed the dominant axis, while paired components encoded pattern phase. Manifold geometry depended on amino-acid chemistry, repeat number, and linker sequence, and collapsed when amino acids were assigned to arbitrary categories. ESM2 therefore combines general repeat recognition with protein-specific physicochemical information. More broadly, synthetic sequence libraries provide experimentally grounded probes of protein language model representations and their relationship to protein biophysics.
n6c683f2a3198: Although SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) show cardiovascular benefits in addition to glycemic control, their molecular target for cardiovascular effect remains unclear. A recent study reported that two SGLT2i, empagliflozin and dapagliflozin, directly activate pantothenate kinase 1 (PANK1), which mediate their cardioprotective effect. PANK1 phosphorylates pantothenate with ATP to yield 4'-phosphopantothenate and ADP, representing the rate-limiting enzyme of coenzyme A (CoA) biosynthesis. We therefore reassessed this claim using purified recombinant human PANK1. The malachite green assay detected free inorganic phosphate (Pi) but neither ADP nor 4'-phosphopantothenate and its signals do not reflect PANK1 activity. In the ADP-Glo assay, empagliflozin and dapagliflozin did not stimulate PANK1 under either basal conditions or acetyl-CoA feedback inhibition, while the activator PZ-2891 enhanced the activity of PANK1. These results show that SGLT2i do not directly activate PANK1, challenging the proposed PANK1-dependent cardioprotection mechanism.
n25bf5fa51069: Neutrophils can promote pathogen control or drive tissue-damaging inflammation, but the mechanisms that determine these divergent outcomes remain poorly defined. COVID-19 and active tuberculosis (TB) offer a purposeful comparison since both are pulmonary infections with substantial neutrophil involvement, yet differ in pathogen class, inflammatory duration, and the balance between neutrophil-associated host defense and pathology. We therefore tested whether their divergent neutrophil programs align with distinct maturation-associated transcriptional states. We integrated six publicly available whole-blood bulk RNA-sequencing datasets, comprising three COVID-19 and three active TB cohorts. A curated panel of 770 genes covered activation, degranulation, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, chemotaxis, cell surface receptors, and maturation. Study-associated variation was reduced using ComBat-Seq, and differential expression relative to disease-appropriate controls was assessed with DESeq2. Most genes changed in the same direction in both diseases, but 348 (45.2%) differed significantly in response magnitude, with 159 genes showing a stronger response in COVID-19 and 189 in TB. COVID-19 samples showed reduced expression of the maturation markers CD10 (MME) and CD16 (FCGR3A), alongside elevated expression of granule-cargo and NET-associated genes, including MPO and ELANE, consistent with a greater contribution from immature, emergency granulopoiesis-derived neutrophil populations. In contrast, TB samples showed higher maturation-associated, receptor, oxidative, and recruitment responses, consistent with a relatively mature receptor-competent neutrophil transcriptional signature. Independent COVID-19 Ward and pulmonary TB cohorts showed directional agreement for maturation and NET-associated signatures (100% and 90% concordance, respectively), while chemotaxis and select receptor and degranulation genes showed weaker reproducibility indicating that maturation represents the most consistently reproduced axis of distinction between the two diseases. Together, these findings identify maturation-associated transcription as the most consistently reproduced axis distinguishing COVID-19 from TB. These signatures provide candidate biomarkers for future studies linking neutrophil states to clinical outcomes and informing host-directed therapeutic strategies that preserve antimicrobial function while limiting immunopathology.
nd5d623013d76: Mutational signatures are characteristic patterns of somatic alterations in cancer genomes. A single aberrant mechanism can simultaneously generate coordinated patterns of alterations across multiple mutation modalities, including single-base substitutions (SBSs), doublet-base substitutions (DBSs), and small insertions and deletions (IDs). However, these signatures are typically inferred separately and linked post hoc, obscuring their shared underlying mechanisms. To resolve this, we formally define a Mutational Process (MP) as a unified latent activity that induces coupled mutational signatures across these modalities. We developed MOTET, a Bayesian framework that jointly infers multimodal MPs. Applied to 2,583 whole genomes from the PCAWG cohort, MOTET recovers known MPs more accurately than standard post hoc correlation methods. MOTET also identifies a process linking an SBS37-related signature with a TG>CA-dominated DBS component and resolves canonical SBS12-like activity into two separate MPs with distinct tissue distributions. These results establish a paradigm for formally defining catalogs of MPs and demonstrate that integrating across modalities enhances the ability to discover new mutational patterns.
nd8fe247d1b8e: A protein's sequence says what a gene could do in another species; the cells of that species say what it does there. Comparative genomics measures the first. Chimera measures the second, a gene's deployment, on the same genes and reports the difference. It aligns single-cell atlases across species in one generative model and returns, for every one-to-one ortholog, the evidence in the counts for a shared expression pattern, and {Delta}[a], the position of that evidence above or below what the protein's identity predicts. This difference is not sequence constraint under another name: across eight tissues, protein identity tracks dN/dS, whereas {Delta}[a] tracks neither. A gene therefore has two coordinates, not one, and the second can contradict the first: spermatocyte genes such as ZPBP2 keep their stage pattern on less conserved proteins, in eight held-out species, whereas conserved hepatocyte enzymes such as ALAS1 share their pattern but not their level. More broadly, genes of specialized cells sit above what their proteins predict in 23 of 24 cohorts, and approved drug targets do so more often than matched genes. Even among nearly identical proteins, where sequence can no longer tell genes apart, the count evidence still does. Nor does this rest on the model alone: independent data support the count evidence in liver and testis and, in a pre-specified test, {Delta}[a] in liver. With both coordinates, one can ask whether another species uses a gene as humans do, the premise of every animal model of a disease gene or drug target.
n0d65343ae16a: Background. Noncoding variants account for over 90% of genome-wide association study (GWAS) findings, but their mechanisms are often unclear. Sequence-to-function models provide one approach to variant interpretation by predicting the effects of genetic variation on molecular phenotypes. ChromBPNet predicts variant effects on chromatin accessibility, but how these predictions are organized across differentiation hierarchies and relate to orthogonal predictions remains unclear. Results. We trained ChromBPNet models for 17 hematopoietic cell types and scored 302,830 variants. Of 242,307 variants accessible in at least one cell type, 5.6% were predicted to alter chromatin accessibility. Variants active in more cell types had larger predicted effects. Predicted effects also reflected hematopoietic lineage structure, with sharing declining with lineage distance while effect direction was preserved in 99.6% of parent-child comparisons. ChromBPNet predictions agreed with GWAS fine-mapping but largely identified distinct variants. Fine-mapping-only variants were enriched for coding and transcript-associated variation, whereas ChromBPNet-only variants were enriched for regulatory elements, accessible chromatin, and trait-relevant activity. In K562 CRISPRi datasets, predicted accessibility gain showed limited association with target-gene validation. Regulatory elements containing CTCF motifs were less likely to have validated target genes, consistent with a role in chromatin organization rather than gene activation. Conclusions. ChromBPNet and fine-mapping provide complementary information about variant function. Predicted accessibility effects identify the cell types in which noncoding variants are likely to act and capture relationships across the hematopoietic hierarchy, but provide limited information about the genes they regulate. All predictions are available at: https://bloodnnet.ccbr.utoronto.ca/. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Evans Leaders Fund and the Ontario Research Fund Small Infrastructure Fund, 46612
n93d51b291105: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) remains a substantial global challenge, with notable individual and sex differences. Heart rate variability (HRV) offers a potential link into the autonomic system underlying alcohol drinking. While simpler, time-domain HRV metrics have been explored, non-linear indicators could provide unique insights into more complex states like compulsive drinking, intake that persists despite negative consequences. We examined heart rate traces from male and female rats during intake of alcohol-only and alcohol+10mg/L quinine, a putative compulsive drinking model. In particular, we re-analyzed previously published findings, but newly focused on several non-linear HRV metrics: the Poincare ratio (possibly reflecting sympathovagal balance) and MultiScale entropy (MSE, perhaps reflecting unpredictability in broader and narrower time windows), along with the previously unexamined spectral HRV metrics (the parasympathetic indictor high-frequency HRV, HF-HRV%). HRV was assessed for the first ~1100 heart beats (~2.5 minutes), to assess HRV correlates of greater alcohol front-loading while having approximately similar amount of data per session. Lower Poincare ratio and higher HF-HRV% were overall related to higher alcohol consumption. In contrast, compulsive drinking, but not alcohol-only, was associated with lower broader-window HRV entropy, which was more pronounced in males. Drinking- and sex-related patterns were further identified using Principle Component Analysis, Ordinary Least Squares, and Linear Mixed Models. Limitations included perhaps being underpowered to detect significant relationships, especially in females. Thus, our preliminary findings suggest that combining HRV metrics could represent useful biomarkers for consumption levels during front-loading, which distinguished general intake from compulsion.
n765b191ee9fa: Membrane contact sites between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and other organelles coordinate cellular organization, metabolism and stress responses, yet how these interfaces are selectively remodeled and removed remains poorly understood. Here we identify a selective autophagy pathway that targets defined ER-mitochondria contact-site (ERMCS) subdomains for turnover, a process we term Contact-phagy. The ER-resident chaperone SIGMAR1 forms a functional complex with the ER-phagy receptor CCPG1, and SIGMAR1-CCPG1 nanoclusters define ERMCS-associated sites of autophagy initiation. Contact-phagy is selectively engaged by metabolic and mitochondrial stress and promotes turnover of defined contact-site components without broadly affecting general ER-phagy, mitophagy or bulk autophagy. At these sites, SIGMAR1-CCPG1 function is coupled to mitochondrial fission: MFF promotes DRP1 recruitment to ERMCS, whereas loss of CCPG1 or SIGMAR1 causes abnormal persistence and clustering of DRP1 and MFF, accompanied by altered mitochondrial remodeling. Loss of CCPG1 further disrupts ER-mitochondria organization and mitochondrial function in pancreatic tissue, while pancreatic cancer cells depend on CCPG1 and SIGMAR1 for organelle integrity and bioenergetic capacity. Together, our findings establish Contact-phagy as a selective pathway for the turnover of defined organelle contact site subdomains and suggest a broader principle by which interorganelle interfaces are maintained.
nf80a90b490a3: Purpose: Morning and evening chronotypes may receive light at different clock times, thereby providing differently timed signals to the circadian pacemaker. Prior studies have suggested phase-specific exposure patterns that could counter further advances in early types and delays in late types. We examined whether photoperiod modifies these exposure patterns in a way that could reasonably counteract timing extremes. Methods: We analysed near-eye melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (EDI) in 140 participants from an international cohort across seven countries (778 participant-days; 35,949 half-hour observations). We compared four quartiles of midsleep on free days corrected for sleep debt (MSF sc ) in clock time and relative to MSF sc using cyclic generalized additive mixed models, accounting for day type, site, photoperiod and individual patterns. In exploratory analyses, we tested moderation of these differences by daylength and used phase-response-curve (PRC) weighting as a conceptual comparison of exposure timing. Results: The modelled extreme evening-type/morning-type exposure ratios averaged 0.16 (95% CI 0.06–0.40) 9.6–11.3 hours before MSF sc (pre-MSF sc ) and 14.0 (5.6–34.8) 0.9–4.4 hours after MSF sc (post-MSF sc ). The models performed similarly well by ordinary in-sample R 2 (0.795 for clock time; 0.794 for MSF sc -relative time). Pattern differences were broadly similar on work and free days, with the pre-MSF sc contrast descriptively attenuated on free days. The post-MSF sc ratio increased by a factor of 2.59 (95% CI 1.06–6.34) between civil photoperiods one hour below and above each site's average photoperiod, with no significant moderation of the pre-MSF sc contrast. Exploratory weighting by the published PRC gave higher advance-weighted point estimates in extreme evening than extreme morning types; the group difference was not statistically significant. Conclusions: Extreme chronotypes differ in daily exposure both in clock time and relative to MSF sc . The established questionnaire-based MSF sc measure showed significant post-MSF sc daylength moderation. The exposure patterns and conceptual PRC comparison suggest a possible pathway linking daylight availability to entrainment in extreme chronotypes.
n0aa0fa77a4ef: One of the longest-standing arguments in evolutionary biology is that between Darwin and Wallace on the evolution of sexual dichromatism, and which sex changed colour over time. While Darwin argued that males became more colourful over time, Wallace argued that females became less colourful, and numerous studies have lent support to each hypothesis over time. Iridescent colouration provides a particularly interesting system for studying sexual dichromatism because its conspicuousness is often associated with sexual selection and it has evolved multiple times. Here, using a dataset on iridescent colouration of 25,432 patches from 3,151 bird species, we provide one of the most comprehensive tests to date of the evolutionary origins of sexual dichromatism. We show that both hypotheses explain the evolution of iridescent sexual dichromatism in birds, but that Darwin's hypothesis is more strongly supported with males contributing stronger to evolutionary changes in dichromatism. Furthermore, our analyses support Darwin's prediction that sexual selection is associated to the evolution of dichromatism, but also Wallace's prediction that safer nests facilitate more colourful females (and males), and mostly in patches exposed during incubation. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n20a3fae1fde2: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) silence target genes through RISC-mediated hybridization and cleavage, but can silence unintended transcripts and cause toxicity or complicate regulatory approval. In drug development, empirical assessment by qPCR and RNA-seq is slow, forces early candidate prioritization, and is limited by available species- and genome-appropriate cell models. While extensive empirical screening remains standard practice, there is a significant opportunity for modern AI methods to change this paradigm. We introduce DeepRNAi, a deep learning model that accurately predicts on- and off-target knockdown from siRNA and mRNA sequence. Trained on 16 million siRNA-transcript pairs from 2,031 siRNAs designed to interrogate known siRNA failure modes, and incorporating transcript context from biological foundation models, DeepRNAi is the first in silico method that approaches experimental accuracy. It generalizes across cell models, transcripts, genomes and species, and in a small study distinguishes approved therapeutics from hepatotoxic candidates. The value of DeepRNAi for prioritizing better candidates up front improving likelihood of success later in development is evidenced by a genome-wide survey of 24.4 million siRNAs targeting 7,946 genes, which indicates that 90.1% of the 100 most potent siRNAs have at least some off-target concerns. To support the community, we are publishing a training and benchmark dataset containing 1.84 million siRNA-transcript pairs from 240 siRNAs.
n0132542a361b: Introduction Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO) is a metabolic disorder, characterized by accelerated bone loss, gut microbiota (GM) dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites. Deoxycholic acid (DCA) is a secondary bile acid with an FDA-approved drug status for submental fat treatment in adults; however its effect on bone health remains underexplored. Materials and Methods This study investigated the effects of DCA on bone health using both preclinical animal model of PMO and clinical samples from PMO women. DCA (20 mg/kg) was administered to ovariectomised (OVX) mice for 45 days, and its effects on bone microarchitecture and serum cytokines were analysed. Osteoclastogenesis and osteoblastogenesis were evaluated using murine and human samples. Untargeted and targeted metabolomics analyses were performed using an ultra-high-performance liquid chromatographic system coupled with high-resolution Orbitrap mass spectrometry (HRMS). Secondary analysis of 16S rRNA sequencing data was performed using R programming. Results GM analysis and plasma metabolomics revealed an alteration in bacterial taxa associated with secondary BA synthesis and reduced circulating DCA levels. DCA administration improved impaired trabecular and cortical bone microarchitecture in the OVX mice by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis and enhancing osteoblastogenesis. Moreover, DCA altered circulating osteoclastogenic (IL-6, Il-9, IL-17A, IFN-γ, RANKL) and osteoblastogenic (OPG, TGF-β, IL-10) factors. Mechanically, DCA suppressed osteoclast differentiation and the expression of genes associated with osteoclast formation (NFATC1, NFΚB, TRAF6, TREM2, SYNB), fusion (CSF1R, DC-STAMP, CD47), and resorption (CTSK, ATP6VOD1, ATP6VOD2, CAR2, SPP1) in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), while promoting osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization in bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) from PMO women. Additionally, DCA enhanced the nascent calcium deposition at the fracture site and improved bone healing via inhibiting osteoclastogenesis. Conclusion Overall, reduced DCA availability was associated with PMO, while DCA treatment mitigated OVX-induced bone loss and improved bone healing. This study highlights the therapeutic potential of DCA for maintaining both bone homeostasis in PMO and fracture healing with immense orthopaedic applications. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nf7709f0dc012: African swine fever virus (ASFV) is a large, complex DNA virus that causes a severe haemorrhagic disease in domestic swine and Eurasian wild boar. Due to its high pathogenicity, research involving ASFV is restricted to high-containment laboratories, which significantly limits investigations into its biology, host interactions and the development of effective control measures. To overcome these limitations, this study utilised pseudotyped virus (PV) technology to identify ASFV proteins involved in cell entry. Candidate proteins were identified through bioinformatic analysis and a review of the published literature, incorporated into PVs, and subsequently assessed for their ability to facilitate cellular entry. This approach identified a combination of three ASFV proteins that, when combined, resulted in the most efficient cell entry. This work represents the successful generation of the first functional ASF pseudotype system for both Ba71v and Georgia 2007 strains, enabling the safe study of ASFV entry mechanisms under containment level 2.
nad4d6e495942: Working memory (WM) requires neural circuits to change how they interact as information is encoded, maintained and used. Directional oscillatory interactions in the medial temporal lobe (MTL) contribute to memory processing, but how these interactions are spatially organized during verbal WM remains unclear. Here, we analyzed intracranial electroencephalogram and neuronal spiking recorded from the human MTL during a verbal Sternberg task. Theta- and gamma-band activities in MTL showed predominant directionality in the posterior-to-anterior axis during WM encoding, but this direction was reversed to anterior-to-posterior during retrieval. Theta activities reflecting the WM load were more prevalent in left than right MTL, and theta in left MTL coordinated spike timings more strongly. Moreover, interhemispheric interactions showed a predominant left-to-right influence, with posterior-to-anterior interactions enhanced during encoding and anterior-to-posterior interactions enhanced during retrieval. Together, these findings suggest that verbal WM engages a spatially organized MTL network in which the predominant direction of oscillatory interactions changes across task phases.
ne680221836c8: Pathogenic germinal center (GC) activity persists in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) because current B cell-targeting therapies do not consistently eliminate the resilient GC niche that sustains autoimmunity. Complement receptor 2 (CR2/CD21) presents a unique bicellular therapeutic target to impede GC-associated autoimmune disease. For B cells, it has been previously shown to lower the threshold for B cell activation, and for follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), it sustains the GC response. Using a CD21-blocking antibody in a spontaneous lupus-prone mouse model, we demonstrate that dual CD21 blockade on both B cells and FDCs synergistically inhibited GC B cell responses and suppressed autoantibody production, memory recall, and renal antibody deposition. Mechanistically, B cell-specific blockade impaired GC entry by limiting initial activation, whereas FDC-specific blockade disrupted GC architecture and curtailed ongoing responses. Further, dual blockade uniquely reshaped immunological memory by promoting accumulation of a CD21low/-CD38+ memory B cell subset with attenuated antibody-secreting cell (ASC) recall potential. These findings identify CD21 blockade as a precision immunomodulatory strategy capable of suppressing pathogenic humoral immunity without complete B cell depletion.
nacae713e9431: Predicting how mutations impact protein function and stability remains a key challenge in computational biology. Current state-of-the-art protein language models (PLMs) primarily scale parameter size on sequence corpora to capture evolutionary constraints but remain blind to the explicit physical dynamics of folded proteins. Conversely, models trained strictly on physical dynamics neglect critical evolutionary sequence statistics. In this paper, we bridge this gap by introducing DynamicsPLM, a highly parameter-efficient 35-million-parameter model that unifies evolutionary and biophysical representation learning. Utilizing a second-stage, multi-task continual pretraining strategy on over 60,000 proteins, we enrich a foundational sequence encoder with explicit residue-level and pairwise molecular dynamics heads while preserving its original evolutionary knowledge. At inference, DynamicsPLM computes zero-shot mutation effects from sequence alone by balancing an evolutionary plausibility score against a structural dynamics disruption score. Across the massive ProteinGym benchmark and natural variants of the Tsuboyama folding stability dataset, DynamicsPLM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among all models under 100M parameters, and matches or outperforms several billion-scale sequence-based models of its size. Our findings demonstrate that explicit structural-dynamics supervision provides a parameter-efficient alternative to raw scale. Availability: All codes including data preparation scripts, training and validation recipes, and experimental configurations for LoMuS are available at: https://github.com/kabir-ai2bio-lab/DynamicsPLM.
n07e8cbf360d1: The extracellular matrix (ECM) is increasingly recognized as both a hallmark of aging and a durable record of the cellular stress states that shape age-related tissue dysfunction. Despite its apparent role in aging and disease, translating matrisome gene expression into interpretable biological meaning remains an unresolved challenge. Here we introduce ECMExplainer, a framework that uses 180 matrisome gene-pair ratios, partitioned into 76 Assembly/Destruction and 104 Signaling/Signaling pairs to position fibroblast transcriptomes within a functional matrisome phenotype space defined by six reference fibroblast states spanning physiological and stress-associated conditions: Proliferating, Quiescence, Senescence, Fibrosis, Inflammation, and Hypoxia. Because each ratio records only which of the two genes is more highly expressed, it is largely insensitive to sequencing depth and batch offsets, allowing ECMExplainer to outperform magnitude-based classifiers on unseen data. Rather than assigning only a single phenotype label, ECMExplainer measures a sample's coordinate distance to each reference state, enabling quantitative mapping of matrisome state trajectories while giving biological meaning even to conditions that fall between or outside the training phenotypes. Across 20 independent fibroblast datasets, ECMExplainer uncovered conserved ECM signatures underlying diverse fibroblast states and showed that they capture multiple aging-related processes. Specifically, it identified FST/ITGA1 as a rapamycin-sensitive senescence-associated ratio, revealed a fibrosis-biased ECM trajectory in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome distinct from chronological aging, and distinguished successful from failed OSKM reprogramming using an ECM Aging Score without retraining. Together, these findings establish the matrisome as a compact and biologically interpretable carrier of cellular state information, and ECMExplainer as a quantitative foundation for interpreting aging, fibrosis and rejuvenation through the lens of the ECM. ### Competing Interest Statement RAA is the Chief Scientific Officer (CSO) of Sustayn Bioscience GmbH. JSPS Kakenhi, 25H01053 Grant-in-Aid Transformative Research Areas (A) Multimodal ECM, 23H04927, 23H04928 RIKEN BDR Life-Cycle Redesign Project German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, FKZ 03EGTMV007
nf3985a38bb30: Human cognition and neurological disorders reflect properties of distributed networks, yet how best to engage these networks therapeutically remains unknown. Multisite stimulation is a principled strategy for engaging brain networks, but a key translational barrier is understanding how a network combines concurrent inputs from multiple nodes. Here, we investigated the electrophysiology of simultaneous multisite direct electrical stimulation in 20 participants implanted with stereo-EEG electrodes. Synchronized dual-site stimulation engaged a larger effective network than single-site stimulation. Linear superposition explained most responses, but distinct nonlinear responses were also observed. Sublinear responses, consistent with saturation, occurred proximal to stimulation sites, while supralinear responses arose in network-connected sites during the response's late component. Moreover, low-intensity dual-site stimulation matched or exceeded single-site stimulation at higher intensities. These principles extended to three-site stimulation. These findings systematically characterize how responses to simultaneous multisite stimulation interact in the human brain, a foundational step towards principled, network-guided neurostimulation therapies.
nf05a3979e203: Yarrowia lipolytica is an important host for biotechnology and metabolic engineering, valued for its ability to accumulate lipids and produce a wide range of industrially relevant compounds. This creates a growing need for genome-scale tools that can accelerate the identification of genes underlying complex phenotypes. Although Cas9-based CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) and activation (CRISPRa) tools are well established in Y. lipolytica, Cas12a offers a complementary platform with a T-rich PAM that can expand access to promoter regions and facilitate multiplexed regulation. Despite these advantages, Cas12a-based CRISPRi/a remains comparatively underdeveloped in Y. lipolytica, particularly for large-scale functional screening. Here, we establish and systematically benchmark dCas12a-based CRISPRi/a platforms for pooled screening in Y. lipolytica. We first compared two widely used effectors, dLbCas12a and denAsCas12a, across single-gene assays and a pooled CRISPRi library targeting nine essential or conditionally essential genes with 752 crRNAs. Both orthologs supported robust transcriptional repression, but their relative performance was crRNA- and condition-dependent, with dLbCas12a showing more consistent and stronger late-stage depletion across targets. dLbCas12a also enabled enrichment-based CRISPRi and CRISPRa screens, recovering expected drug-resistance and lipid-associated phenotypes. The broad design of the pooled library further enabled identification of crRNA features associated with CRISPRi efficacy. Highly active crRNAs were enriched near transcription start sites, with an effective targeting interval extending from approximately -260 to +50 bp. Intermediate GC content was associated with higher efficacy, while PAM identity showed a weaker but consistent effect, with TTTA and TTTT PAMs linked to stronger depletion than TTTC and TTTG PAMs. Spacer length showed the strongest association with CRISPRi efficacy, with 18-nt crRNAs consistently outperforming matched longer 20-, 23-, and 25-nt variants. Finally, we tested dHyperLbCas12a, an engineered LbCas12a variant with enhanced activity, and found that it produced substantially stronger CRISPRi and CRISPRa phenotypes than dLbCas12a. Together, these results establish Cas12a as a versatile platform for pooled CRISPRi/a screens in Y. lipolytica, identify practical crRNA prioritization rules for improved library performance, and highlight dHyperLbCas12a as a promising effector for future large-scale gain- and loss-of-function screens.
n2edd3c2930ac: Bacterial extracellular vesicles (EVs) are an ancestral secretion route that delivers cargoes to host cells. Although rhizobial EVs transport Nod factors and other bacterial components, their role in protein delivery during symbiosis remains unexplored. Here we characterise EveD, a large soluble repeat-containing protein of Sinorhizobium fredii HH103. Its export is independent of the type III secretion system, and EveD is recovered only in EV-containing fractions. eveD expression is not induced by genistein or soybean seed exudates and does not follow the canonical NodD1-TtsI pathway, but partially depends on the symbiotic regulator SyrM. When expressed in plant cells, EveD localises mainly to the cytoplasm, associates with endoplasmic reticulum-like structures and occasionally occurs in the nucleus. The eveD mutant shows increased nodule occupancy relative to the wild type in Glycine max cv. Williams 82. EveD modulates early responses in wild Glycine soja accessions in a genotype-dependent manner, constraining pseudonodule organogenesis in JL2 while promoting it in CH2. These findings identify EveD as an EV-associated rhizobial protein contributing to bacterial competitiveness and genotype-dependent symbiotic responses, and highlight EVs as an additional route for protein export during legume symbiosis.
n03af8fb6feb2: Bacteriophage proteins evolve through extensive modular exchange, yet the sequence units underlying this process remain poorly defined. Classical domains are plausible evolutionary modules, but they incompletely annotate phage proteins and may not always coincide with the regions conserved across protein families. Here, we constructed 13,035 Evolutionarily Conserved Fragments (ECFs), grouped into 3,167 families, through large-scale HMM-HMM comparisons of proteins from 5,396 RefSeq phage genomes, without imposing predefined domain boundaries. ECFs overlapped substantially with ECOD and Pfam annotations but formed a heterogeneous spectrum comprising subdomains, domain-equivalent units, composite regions and fragments with no counterpart in either resource. Their relationships were frequently nested, indicating that conserved modules occur at multiple organisational scales. ECFs annotated 50% of phage representative proteins (at least doubling the coverage of either database), with the largest gains in structural and infection-related functions, a pattern replicated in independent metagenomic data. ECF families also showed function-dependent patterns of diversity and spatial segregation and provided functional associations for 23,925 protein families lacking detectable Pfam or ECOD domains. In receptor-binding proteins, ECFs subdivided established domains, delineated previously unannotated structural elements and recovered homologous regions where structural similarity was ambiguous. These results show that the evolutionary building blocks of phage proteins do not always coincide with classical domains, highlighting that evolutionary processes act across multiple scales. ECFs provide a complementary, sequence-derived framework for investigating how complex viral proteins are assembled, diversified and functionally organised.
n67de6bc180af: Background: Huntington's disease burdens protein homeostasis and affects neurons and glia differently across brain regions, but how these two main cell populations respond as the disease progresses remains unresolved. Whole-tissue proteomes mix these cell types and hide how the proteome of each changes. We therefore measured the proteome of each cell type separately at different disease stages. Methods: We metabolically labelled cell-type-specific proteomes in living R6/1 mice and wild-type littermates for 15 days at different disease stages. We examined cortical and hippocampal excitatory neurons at 1.5, 3 and 7 months, cerebellar inhibitory neurons at 3 and 7 months, and cortical, striatal and cerebellar glia at 7 months. We combined mass spectrometry with functional enrichment and competitive protein-set tests to understand the differential proteostatic response to mutant huntingtin across disease progression, brain regions and cell types. Differential abundance was tested with a peptide-centric linear mixed model (msqRob, Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.1), and proteins whose levels varied together in cortical and hippocampal neurons were grouped into modules by weighted correlation network analysis. Results: Hippocampal excitatory neurons showed broader and more coordinated regulation than cortical neurons already before motor onset, whereas the cortical response increased with age and no cortical protein module differed between genotypes before the most severe stage. All three neuronal populations upregulated ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) proteins as the disease advanced. Protein folding changed, with more subunits of the chaperonin CCT/TRiC but fewer J-domain proteins and, in excitatory neurons, fewer HSP70 chaperones. At the most severe stage, glia of the three studied regions regulated mainly different proteins, but all increased UPS proteins and decreased key proteins of neuronal support, among them the main glial glutamate transporter GLT-1. Cholesterol-related proteins decreased in cortical and cerebellar glia, and respiratory-chain proteins in striatal glia. Conclusions: Synaptic proteins decreased early in cortical and hippocampal neurons and were not restored at later ages. A later and broader maintenance response coexisted with their continued and increasing downregulation. In this first cell-type-resolved view of the labelled proteome in a Huntington's disease mouse model, progression appears as a change in the coordination of cellular functions, which whole-tissue measurements would dilute.
n9cbef8117df0: Background: Germline-targeting HIV-1 vaccination recruits VRC01-class B-cell precursors, but the positional patterns of observed longitudinal B-cell receptor lineage-state changes remain incompletely described. We compared CDRH2 profiles between homologous and heterologous boosting regimens using published IAVI G002 data. Methods: Participant-specific Week-8 lineages were prospectively matched to Week-24 observations. Germline-to-nongermline changes in sampled lineage-modal residues were evaluated at seven IGHV1-2*02 CDRH2 positions using participant-balanced, mean-centered profiles and exact participant-label permutation inference. Sampling-depth and sorting-probe sensitivity analyses assessed observability. A separate participant-held-out benchmark evaluated antibody-language-model representations for predicting observed Week-24 lineage detection. Results: The CDRH2 analysis included 332 lineages, 15 participants, 2,179 eligible lineage-position observations, and 241 observed state changes. The regional profile statistic was 0.027066 (exact p = 0.001709; six-region adjusted q = 0.010256), with descriptive differences at V-relative positions 51, 54, and 55. Most eligible longitudinal observations had one assessable cell per visit. In seven Group-1 participants, Week-24 dual-probe sampling recovered 181 baseline lineages with eOD-GT8 and 143 with Cg28v2, including 60 detected by both probes. In a separate cohort of 2,739 lineages from 17 participants, IgBERT and AbLang-2 representations did not improve participant-balanced average precision over a four-feature biological baseline. Conclusions: Observed CDRH2 lineage-modal-state profiles differed between regimens in this exploratory secondary analysis. Sparse sampling, potentially probe-related ascertainment, and absent linked functional validation preclude inference about mutation timing, functional improvement, or causal booster effects.
nae675f03bfb5: Marine sponges (phylum Porifera) are a highly diverse and polymorphic group of marine invertebrates whose taxonomic delimitation is often challenging due to high intraspecific variability and the scarcity of diagnostic morphological characters. Their close association with microbial symbionts also makes them an important source of secondary metabolites, some of which may contribute to sponge colouration. Here, we use morphological characters, molecular phylogenetic markers, and 16S metabarcoding of the symbiont community to understand speciation in a common Mediterranean sponge lineage. We collected 43 specimens of the genus Suberites from the Mediterranean Sea and the North and South Atlantic Oceans, between 55-150 m depths, and sequenced two barcoding genes, cytochrome c oxidase I and 28S rDNA, as well as studied their spicular complements. We identified five closely-related species: S. domuncula , S. ficus/pagurorum , S. dandelenae , S. ambulodomus , and a new species of Suberites from the Balearic Islands, Suberites sp. nov. The latter represents a potential new pseudo-cryptic species closely related to S. domuncula , because of their strong morphological and molecular affinities. The potential new Mediterranean species exhibits six colour morphotypes (yellow, gray, orange, brown, red, and blue), and the microbiome analyses of the symbiotic communities revealed significant differences in bacterial community composition among colour morphotypes, specially of bacteria that produce different pigments which potentially give the sponge is colouration. These results provide valuable insights into species boundaries and evolutionary relationships within the genus Suberites and support a role for the microbiome in sponge colouration.
n2a91e3c89d55: RNA binding proteins (RBPs) serve as upstream master regulators of cellular fate transitions at the post-transcriptional level. RBP-RNA interactions are dynamically regulated by post-translational modifications to coordinate cellular responses. We hypothesised that changes in RBP phosphorylation will play a key role in coordinating angiogenesis, the formation of new blood vessels, in endothelial cells (ECs). Therefore, we used phospho-proteomic analysis of the mRNA bound proteome to identify global phosphorylation changes in mouse cardiac ECs during acute and prolonged VEGF-A stimulation. Of the differentially phosphorylated RBPs, we found that the phosphorylation of serine 199 within mRNA bound Phf6 (PHD finger protein 6) was consistently increased following VEGF-A stimulation. Phf6 phosphorylation at this specific site was sufficient and required to induce a pro-angiogenic phenotype, facilitating a change in Phf6 conformation promoting interaction with distinct RNAs. We show here that Phf6 phosphorylation at serine 199, downstream of VEGF-A, acts as a molecular switch to differentially coordinate a decrease of anti-angiogenic RNAs (i.e. extracellular matrix genes) and an increase in pro-angiogenesis related RNAs, in part by differentially regulating their stability, to promote angiogenesis.
nd63c167f909f: Perturb-seq enables systematic interrogation of massively parallel genetic perturbations at single-cell resolution, yet exhaustive characterization of the full perturbation space remains impractical. Here, we present Graph-guided Flow Matching (GFM), a generative framework that integrates biological knowledge graphs with latent flow matching to predict post-perturbation single-cell transcriptomes. Across multiple large-scale Perturb-seq datasets, GFM outperforms a strong linear baseline and current deep-learning models in predicting unseen single-gene perturbations, while training up to 30x faster and remaining robust with limited training data. GFM also demonstrates competitive performance in the two-gene perturbation prediction task when neither perturbed gene is observed during training. Ablation experiments show that combining flow matching with knowledge graphs enables accurate prediction of perturbation responses. Finally, GFM accurately calculates transcriptional consequences of HSP90AA1 inactivation and identifies target candidates unseen by the model in chronic myeloid leukemia. Our study establishes GFM as a biologically informed generative framework that predicts single-cell perturbation responses for prioritization of therapeutic targets.
n7bec8c94e7cf: Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate cellular signaling and protein function, making accurate site identification essential for understanding protein regulation. However, PTM site recognition and functional phosphosite prediction are largely modeled independently, limiting the transfer of large-scale recognition knowledge to functional prioritization. Here, we introduce HieraPTM-HieraFuncPhos, a cross-task hierarchical framework that separately models and conditionally integrates transferable PTM recognition representations and function-specific mechanical evidence. HieraPTM integrates local sequence patterns, protein language model representations, and three-dimensional structural information to recognize multiple PTM types. HieraFuncPhos transfers these representations through parameter-efficient adaptation and adaptively retrieves local and distal mechanical evidence conditioned on functional representations. At HSP90AA1 T36 and T115, the model reveals distinct mechanical response patterns consistent with published nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) observations, suggesting that the framework not only prioritizes functional phosphosites but also provides biophysically grounded, testable hypotheses regarding site-specific regulation. HieraPTM achieved macro-averaged AUROC and AUPRC values of 0.9237 and 0.8425 across eight PTM tasks, while maintaining competitive performance on severely imbalanced external benchmarks. HieraFuncPhos achieved an AUROC of 0.8274 and an AUPRC of 0.8188, outperforming existing comparison methods. Together, this framework connects PTM site recognition, functional prioritization, and structure-informed hypotheses regarding potential regulatory processes.
nf4e2eb6db38b: High +Gz exposure elicits complex cardiovascular, autonomic, and endocrine responses, but the associated molecular responses in humans remain poorly understood. We investigated whether microRNAs (miRNAs) encapsulated in urinary extracellular vesicles (uEVs) are altered following acute high +Gz exposure. Twenty-one healthy young men undergoing human centrifuge training provided urine samples before, immediately after, and on the morning after exposure. Candidate uEV-encapsulated miRNAs were identified by RNA sequencing and Gene Ontology analysis, and 16 miRNAs related to ischemia, hypoxia, blood pressure regulation, and mechanical stress were quantified by quantitative PCR. Salivary cortisol, urinary catecholamines, and heart rate were also assessed. Six uEV-encapsulated miRNAs increased significantly after high +Gz exposure. miR-20b-5p, miR-125b-5p, and miR-130a-3p increased immediately after exposure and returned to baseline by the following morning, whereas miR-335-5p, miR-17-5p, and miR-92a-3p remained elevated. Urinary adrenaline, noradrenaline, and dopamine increased immediately after exposure; adrenaline returned to baseline by the following morning, whereas noradrenaline and dopamine remained elevated. Salivary cortisol and heart rate also increased. These findings demonstrate distinct transient and sustained temporal responses of uEV-encapsulated miRNAs to high +Gz in humans, paralleling different catecholamine response patterns. Although their tissue origins and functional roles remain unresolved, these findings provide new molecular-level insights into the human physiological response to high +Gz.
n42957c38298a: Conformational dynamics of biomolecules, including proteins and nucleic acids, are often coupled to changes in protonation states. All-atom particle-mesh Ewald continuous constant-pH molecular dynamics (PME-CpHMD) enables proton-coupled dynamics, but its routine use has been limited by computational cost. Here we report a second-generation CUDA implementation of PME-CpHMD in Amber, in which the CpHMD-specific nonbonded corrections are evaluated in a separate kernel. Across protein systems ranging from 45 to 1,338 residues, the new implementation increases throughput by 1.5-2 fold relative to the previous fused-kernel implementation and limits the overhead relative to conventional MD to 12-18%. We also implemented the asynchronous pH replica-exchange (pH-REX) algorithm natively in pmemd.cuda.MPI, allowing simulations to run on fewer GPUs than replicas without the overhead of the previous Python wrapper. Furthermore, we derived CpHMD titration parameters for all six titratable residue types (Asp, Glu, His, Cys, Tyr, and Lys) for use with three protein force fields: CHARMM c22/CMAP, Amber ff14sb and ff19sb. The new implementations and parameterization were validated using pKa calculations of model peptides and hen egg white lysozyme (HEWL). The HEWL simulations revealed force-field-specific limitations, including overestimation of the pKa downshift 20 of H15 and sensitivity of the proton donor assignment in coupled E35/D52 dyad. Comparison with our previous work and the PME-CpHMD simulations in GROMACS with the CHARMM c36m force field demonstrated the robustness and sampling efficiency of pH-REX PME-CpHMD simulations. The new implementation provides a foundation for routine all-atom constant-pH simulations in Amber. The analysis highlights the need for continued development of protein force fields to more accurately balance intramolecular electrostatics and solvation of charged residues.
n178910f45013: Large-scale neural recordings increasingly span many sessions, brain regions and animals, but differences in neuronal sampling make it difficult to identify and interpret shared patterns. We introduce Neuralign, a tensor- based model that jointly aligns and decomposes recordings into components, each pairing a shared temporal pattern with its expression in individual trials and neurons, without requiring matched neurons, matched trials or behavioural labels. In simulations, pooling recordings improved recovery of shared components; in recurrent networks, Neuralign distinguished related from distinct task solutions. In the macaque motor cortex, label-free components recovered the ring-like organisation of reach directions. Across 93 brain-wide mouse recordings, Neuralign discovered a single component that isolated the response to inhibition of the anterior lateral motor cortex (ALM). A reference learned from correct, uninhibited trials revealed inhibition-related activity outside the choice direction on error trials, most strongly in the ALM and thalamus. Neuralign provides an interpretable framework for studying the shared structure of large neural datasets, linking shared patterns to individual trials and recorded populations.
n7b1f5e78eb2e: Alterations in central cholinergic systems are implicated in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We previously identified TSHZ3 as an ASD-linked gene and provided evidence, from transgenic mouse models, supporting the view that striatal cholinergic interneurons (SCINs) are key players in the core ASD trait represented by repetitive behaviors (RBs). Indeed, conditional deletion of Tshz3 in cholinergic neurons (Chat-cKO model) results in RBs associated with reduced SCIN firing activity and decreased striatal cholinergic tone.
